transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-11-28
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 56 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Jonas Park (Redwood Solutions Eng), Maya Patel (Altair Head of ML), Tom Reynolds (Altair Platform), Hannah Lopez (Altair PM), Omar Idris (Altair Security)

Auto-generated Summary (brief):
- Kickoff to define quality evaluation plan for a 6-week POC: golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination checks, throughput/latency benchmarks, and timelines.
- Customer requires on-prem/VPC option evaluation and SOC2 artifacts.
- Agreed to baseline benchmark plus one quantized run; customer to deliver sample queries and golden examples.

Topics: POC success criteria; throughput & latency targets; golden prompts & goldset; regression gating; hallucination/format checks; scoring rubric; pilot timeline + infra (Hosted vs Dedicated / VPC).

Action items (auto list): see metadata action_items above.

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Okay hi everyone, thanks for joining — this is Alex from Redwood, I think we have about 55, 56 minutes on the calendar. Um, quick roll call?
[00:08] Maya Patel: Hey Alex, Maya here.
[00:09] Tom Reynolds: Tom, hi.
[00:10] Hannah Lopez: Hannah here.
[00:11] Omar Idris: Omar, security.
[00:12] Priya Singh: Priya from the SE team. Jonas is on as well.
[00:16] Jonas Park: yep hi all.
[00:18] Alex Chen: Great. Goal for today: define success criteria for the POC, agree goldset & scoring approach, get rough workload sizing for benchmarks, and align timeline. We'll also surface any security blockers.
[00:30] Maya Patel: Our team is focused on replacing a rules-based product summarization flow with an LLM assist. Key success for us is precision on attribute extraction, stable latency below 300 ms p95, and hallucination rate under 2% on our golden cases. Also total cost per 10k requests should be comparable-ish to current infra.
[00:50] Priya Singh: Good — that gives us measurable targets. When you say 300 ms p95, is that for end-to-end with your front-end or for inference only?
[00:58] Hannah Lopez: We mean inference only, the front end adds about 100 ms.
[01:02] Priya Singh: OK inference-only. Our hosted endpoints typically do 120–250 ms p95 for smaller models and 200–400 for larger ones depending on sequence length. For Dedicated we can tighten that.
[01:18] Tom Reynolds: On traffic, for the pilot we expect bursty peaks: daytime 50 RPS sustained for 30 mins, average around 10 RPS. For production we project 300 RPS steady, but that's future. For the POC please size for 50 RPS with 2x burst headroom.
[01:36] Jonas Park: Noted. For benchmarking we like to do three runs: baseline model (float), quantized model, and a cached-run (prefix cache enabled) to show unit cost improvements. Does that align?
[01:45] Maya Patel: Yes. Also we want to test prompt injection and hallucination scenarios — make sure the model is not inventing SKUs or prices.
[01:52] Priya Singh: We'll include a hallucination test suite. Quick note: hallucination thresholds are usually measured against the golden set with exact-match or token-level F1 depending on output type.
[02:05] Hannah Lopez: Can you expand on the goldset? We have a concept of golden prompts and golden outputs — about 30-50 high-value examples?
[02:12] Priya Singh: Ideal goldset for this POC: 50-100 golden prompts that cover edge cases, multi-attribute extraction, and abusive/ambiguous phrasing. Also a larger regression set of ~500 representative customer queries to run at each regression checkpoint.
[02:30] Maya Patel: We can provide 500 queries but only 40-60 golden labeled examples.
[02:34] Priya Singh: That's fine. We'll make a small rubric mapping: for extraction tasks we score by attribute-level precision/recall, and then compute a weighted quality score where extraction correctness is 70%, format compliance 20%, hallucination penalty 10%.
[02:48] Tom Reynolds: Format compliance means JSON schema of returned attributes?
[02:51] Priya Singh: Yes, e.g., keys must be present, types correct, and no extra fields. We'll run structural checks and also a lightweight schema validator.
[02:58] Omar Idris: From security: we need audit logs, customer-managed KMS, and proof that PII is not retained in logs. Can Redwood run in our VPC or provide on-prem option?
[03:08] Alex Chen: Yes, Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem packages. For the POC we can do a private deployment in your dev VPC or a hosted evaluation with SOC2 artifacts. We can also redact logs or disable retention.
[03:19] Omar Idris: Good. We prefer a VPC for the benchmark runs. I need a lambda or IP whitelist and service account details.
[03:25] Tom Reynolds: We'll also want to run a local mock for our TRs and maybe send a subset over VPN.
[03:30] Priya Singh: For benchmarking methodology: we'll run a stable dataset of 500 queries with the same seed, measure latency distribution (p50/p90/p95/p99), throughput at concurrency increments (1, 10, 50), and token cost per response. We'll also measure latency tail with KV cache warm and cold.
[03:45] Maya Patel: How do you measure hallucination? For extraction tasks sometimes it's not obvious if it's hallucination or inference.
[03:52] Priya Singh: We'll define hallucination as the model returning an attribute value not supported by the source text or fabricating entities. For numeric/price fields we can check against ground truth; for fuzzy fields we'll have human review on the goldset. We'll count hallucination incidents per 100 responses and set gating at <2% on goldset.
[04:10] Hannah Lopez: Score computation — can you show a sample?
[04:14] Jonas Park: Quick mock: Attribute correctness (70 pts) computed as average F1 across attributes, format compliance (20 pts) as percent of responses passing schema checks, hallucination penalty up to -20 on the total scaled so the final score is between 0–100. So final quality score = (0.7 * attr_score) + (0.2 * format_score) - (0.1 * hallucination_rate*100) normalized. We can iterate.
[04:36] Maya Patel: Sounds fair. We want pass/fail gating: must be >=85 on goldset to proceed to pilot.
[04:42] Priya Singh: 85 gate noted. If the hosted baseline fails but quantized model passes, we'll document performance/cost tradeoffs.
[04:50] Tom Reynolds: For benchmarks, we need clear SLOs: inference p95 < 300 ms and tail p99 < 800 ms during 50 RPS burst. Also cost target: under $X per 10k requests — we need Redwood to estimate.
[05:02] Alex Chen: We'll run a cost model after we pick model family. We'll share cost-per-10k estimates for each configuration.
[05:07] Maya Patel: Timeline — we need results in 6 weeks for an executive review. 2 weeks to set up & collect goldset, 2 weeks for runs & iterate, 2 weeks for final report. Does that fit your standard POC cadence?
[05:20] Priya Singh: Yes that's standard. Proposed milestones: Week 0-1: dataset + infra prep, Week 2: baseline benchmark, Week 3: model tuning + quantization runs, Week 4: regression gating + hallucination analysis, Week 5: finalize report, Week 6: exec sync.
[05:33] Hannah Lopez: Can you run A/B between our current rules pipeline and Redwood outputs for NPS-style usability?
[05:38] Jonas Park: We can create an A/B harness using your logging hooks; we'll need sample traffic routing and a short run to collect human labels. That's more manual but doable in week 3-4.
[05:48] Omar Idris: On compliance — we need retention turned off for dev logs and a mini audit trail showing KMS usage.
[05:54] Alex Chen: We'll provide an audit artifact and show demo of KMS integration.
[05:58] Maya Patel: Ok next steps recap?
[06:02] Alex Chen: I'll send the security pack + hosted vs dedicated cost breakdown by Dec 1. Priya will put together the goldset template and initial rubric by Dec 3. Maya to provide samples by Dec 6. We'll schedule a 2-hour benchmark window on Dec 10 — are mornings PST fine?
[06:16] Tom Reynolds: Morning PST is fine. We'll aim to have VPC details by Dec 4.
[06:20] Hannah Lopez: I'll coordinate the golden example selection internally.
[06:24] Omar Idris: I'll confirm KMS and retention constraints by Dec 2.
[06:28] Alex Chen: Great. Any other questions on scoring or the regression gating?
[06:32] Maya Patel: One more: what does rollback look like if we detect regression mid-pilot?
[06:36] Priya Singh: We support automatic fallback policies — if quality drops below threshold or latency spikes, traffic can route to a smaller stable model or to your rules pipeline. We'll document the canary thresholds.
[06:46] Jonas Park: Also we'll keep a changelog of model versions and a diff of quality metrics for rollbacks.
[06:52] Maya Patel: Perfect.
[06:54] Alex Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the items in the next 48 hours and get the calendar invites out for the Dec 10 benchmark.
[06:58] Hannah Lopez: Thanks.
[07:00] Meeting ends.

Notes on transcription: minor ASR errors present, some vendor/product names may be spelled phonetically (e.g., "K V cash" for KV cache, "quantizashun" for quantization). Some speaker turns merged.
